BRs control root meristem activity by modulating cell cycle and cell expansion in the root epistem.
BRs are important for maintaining the root meristem size by controlling cell cycle activity and expansion.

(i) brassinosteroids (BR) are required to maintain the coherent gradient of progression in the root meristem, which is essential for normal root meristem size and shape; (ii) BR activity in the epidermal cells is sufficient to control the root meristem size; (iii) BR signaling in the epiderm is transmitted by different components than the BES1 and/or BZR1 transcriptional factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of BR signaling in root growth and development.
the regulation of root meristem size, and how BR signaling controls this process.
the role of BR signaling in the control of cell cycle activity, cell expansion and differentiation in root meristems.

the root epidermal BRs control meristem size via the modulation of the cell cycle, cell expansion and QC and stele cell files.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BRs are necessary for normal meristem size and function by regulating cell division and expansion, and that the signal is transmitted from the epidermal cells to the root meristem.

the epidermal BR perception in Arabidopsis roots controls the root meristem size by regulating the cell cycle activity and the cell expansion in the meristem cells, and this regulation is probably mediated by an epidermal-to-meristem signal.
the BR signal in the epidermal cells of the root meristem controls the balance between cell cycle progression and expansion, which are both required to maintain a normal root meristem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BRs are essential to maintain normal root meristem size by regulating cell cycle activity and expansion.
BRs control root meristem growth through the epidermis and that the epidermis can control the expression level of QC- and stele-enrich genes.
BRs control root growth by modulating cell cycle progression and cell expansion, and that this activity is mediated by the BES1/BZR1 transcription factors.
